title: Affine-test criterion for fpqc descent of algebraic-space morphism properties
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with universes as in [def-weil-size-convention], and let $P$ be an isomorphism-invariant property of morphisms of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Assume: (1) for every finite set $J$, if each $f_j:X_j\to Y_j$ has $P$, then $\coprod_{j\in J} f_j:\coprod_{j\in J}X_j\to\coprod_{j\in J}Y_j$ has $P$, including $J=\varnothing$, so $P(\varnothing\to\varnothing)$ holds; (2) $P(f:X\to Y)$ holds if and only if $P(X\times_Y Z\to Z)$ holds for every affine $S$-scheme $Z$ and every $Z\to Y$; (3) if $Z'\to Z$ is a flat surjective morphism of affine $S$-schemes and $f:X\to Z$ is an algebraic-space morphism, then $P(X\times_ZZ'\to Z')$ implies $P(f)$. Then $P$ is fpqc local on the target: for every morphism $f:X\to Y$ and every fpqc covering $\{Y_i\to Y\}_{i\in I}$ one has $P(f)$ if and only if $P(X\times_Y Y_i\to Y_i)$ for all $i$. Here an fpqc covering of algebraic spaces means that its arrows are flat on etale scheme charts [def-weil-flat-morphism], and that for every affine scheme $T\to Y$ there are finitely many affine schemes $T_j$, flat maps $T_j\to T$ jointly surjective on points, and maps $T_j\to Y_{i(j)}$ over $Y$. Scheme fpqc coverings mean [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]. Surjectivity for algebraic spaces is on field-valued point classes [def-trf-algebraic-space-jointly-surjective-family]. Fibre products are sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]; coproducts are disjoint unions of sheaves. All index sets lie in the stated universes.

proof.text: First derive stability under arbitrary base change from (2). Suppose $P(f:X\to Y)$ and let $W\to Y$ be any algebraic-space morphism. For every affine $T\to W$, the iterated sheaf pullback $(X\times_YW)\times_WT$ is canonically $X\times_YT$: on any scheme test both describe a pair of sections of $X$ and $T$ with the same image in $Y$, and the inverse inserts the image of the $T$-section in $W$. These mutually inverse maps commute with projection to $T$. Hypothesis (2) applied to $f$ gives $P(X\times_YT\to T)$; isomorphism invariance and (2) applied to $X\times_YW\to W$ give its property $P$. The sheaf pullbacks are algebraic spaces by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Taking $W=Y_i$ proves the forward implication.

For the converse assume $P(f_i)$ for every $i$, and fix an arbitrary affine $Z\to Y$. By the fpqc-covering condition explicitly stated in the item, choose a finite set $J$, affine schemes $Z_j$, flat jointly surjective maps $q_j:Z_j\to Z$, and maps $Z_j\to Y_{i(j)}$ over $Y$. Step 1 applied to $f_{i(j)}$ gives $P(X\times_Y Z_j\to Z_j)$: the identification with its iterated pullback is the same pair-of-sections construction of Step 1. It remains to descend these finitely many assertions to $X\times_YZ\to Z$.

Form the scheme coproduct $Z^{\prime}=\coprod_{j\in J}Z_j$ and its induced morphism $q:Z^{\prime}\to Z$ using [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. Write $Z_j\cong\operatorname{Spec}A_j$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-affine-coproduct-spectrum], $Z^{\prime}\cong\operatorname{Spec}(\prod_jA_j)$ is affine. The coprojections are disjoint open immersions covering $Z^{\prime}$. At a point in the $j$-th piece its local ring and the local map induced by $q$ are those for $q_j$, since an open immersion restricts the structure sheaf [def-weil-open-immersion]. Each such local map is flat, hence $q$ is flat by [def-weil-flat-morphism]. For every point of $Z$, joint surjectivity supplies a point of some $Z_j$, whose coprojection supplies a preimage under $q$; thus $q$ is surjective. If $J$ is empty, joint surjectivity forces $Z$ empty, and the empty product gives the empty affine scheme $Z^{\prime}$; flatness is vacuous.

The scheme coproduct $Z^{\prime}$ also represents the coproduct of the sheaves $h_{Z_j}$. Indeed [lem-trf-fppf-sheaf-coproduct-partition] describes a section over any test scheme $T$ as a clopen partition $T=\coprod_jT_j$ and maps $T_j\to Z_j$. Such data give exactly a map $T\to Z^{\prime}$ by gluing the maps to the open pieces; conversely inverse images of the pieces under a map give that partition and those maps. The two constructions are inverse and commute with restriction, including the empty case. Put $B=X\times_YZ^{\prime}$. Apply [lem-trf-set-sheaf-finite-extensivity] to $B\to h_{Z^{\prime}}=\coprod_jh_{Z_j}$. It identifies $B$ with $\coprod_j(B\times_{Z^{\prime}}Z_j)=\coprod_j(X\times_YZ_j)$; the last identification again forgets the redundant $Z^{\prime}$-coordinate. The canonical isomorphism commutes with the arrows to $Z^{\prime}$, since its restriction to each summand is the coprojection followed by the displayed projection. Hence $B\to Z^{\prime}$ is the coproduct of the arrows from Step 2.

proof.text: Apply finite-coproduct closure (1) to the arrows from Step 2. Step 4 and isomorphism invariance give $P(X\times_YZ^{\prime}\to Z^{\prime})$. This arrow is the base change along $q$ of $X\times_YZ\to Z$, by the same pair-of-sections identification as Step 1. Both $Z$ and $Z^{\prime}$ are affine, and $q$ is flat and surjective by Step 3, so hypothesis (3) gives $P(X\times_YZ\to Z)$. Since the affine test $Z\to Y$ was arbitrary, (2) gives $P(f)$. If the refinement is empty, (1) supplies $P(\varnothing\to\varnothing)$, so the same application of (3) still applies. This proves the converse for every index set $I$, including $I=\varnothing$.

lean.statement: theorem fpqc_property_affine_criterion {S : Scheme.{u}} (P : MorphismProperty (AlgebraicSpace S)) [P.RespectsIso] (hcoprod : ∀ (J : Type u) [Finite J] (Xj Yj : J → AlgebraicSpace S) (fj : ∀ j : J, Xj j ⟶ Yj j) (X Y : AlgebraicSpace S) (a : ∀ j : J, Xj j ⟶ X) (b : ∀ j : J, Yj j ⟶ Y) (q : X ⟶ Y), IsColimit (Cofan.mk X.obj (fun j : J ↦ (a j).hom)) → IsColimit (Cofan.mk Y.obj (fun j : J ↦ (b j).hom)) → (∀ j : J, a j ≫ q = fj j ≫ b j) → (∀ j : J, P (fj j)) → P q) (haffine : ∀ (X Y : AlgebraicSpace S) (f : X ⟶ Y), P f ↔ ∀ (Z : Over S) [IsAffine Z.left] (g : schemeSpace Z ⟶ Y), P (enlargedFibreProductFst g f)) (hdesc : ∀ (Z Z' : Over S) [IsAffine Z.left] [IsAffine Z'.left] (g : Z' ⟶ Z), Flat g.left → Surjective g.left → ∀ (X : AlgebraicSpace S) (f : X ⟶ schemeSpace Z), P (enlargedFibreProductFst (ObjectProperty.homMk ⟨yoneda.map g⟩ : schemeSpace Z' ⟶ schemeSpace Z) f) → P f) {I : Type w} {X Y : AlgebraicSpace S} (f : X ⟶ Y) (Yi : I → AlgebraicSpace S) (g : ∀ i : I, Yi i ⟶ Y) (hflat : ∀ i : I, MapIsFlat (g i)) (hrefine : ∀ (T : Over S) [IsAffine T.left] (a : schemeSpace T ⟶ Y), ∃ (n : ℕ) (Tj : Fin n → Over S) (q : ∀ j : Fin n, Tj j ⟶ T) (k : Fin n → I) (b : ∀ j : Fin n, schemeSpace (Tj j) ⟶ Yi (k j)), (∀ j : Fin n, IsAffine (Tj j).left) ∧ (∀ j : Fin n, Flat (q j).left) ∧ (∀ t : T.left, ∃ (j : Fin n) (s : (Tj j).left), (q j).left s = t) ∧ (∀ j : Fin n, b j ≫ g (k j) = (ObjectProperty.homMk ⟨yoneda.map (q j)⟩ : schemeSpace (Tj j) ⟶ schemeSpace T) ≫ a)) : P f ↔ ∀ i : I, P (enlargedFibreProductFst (g i) f)
